2026-11-30.title: Monday after the Sunday of the Visitation · Mar Andrews Shleeha (St Andrew the Apostle)
readings: Until Christ is formed in you
2026-11-30.alt: St Andrew, Apostle, brother of Simon Peter. The Twenty-Five Days' Fast begins tomorrow, 1 December.
2026-11-30.verse: He first found his brother Simon and said to him, “We have found the Messiah” (which is translated Anointed).
theo: Two disciples of John the Baptist hear him say, “Look, here is the Lamb of God!” and follow Jesus. He turns and asks, “What are you looking for?” They answer, “Rabbi, where are you staying?” and he says, “Come and see.” They spend the day with him. One of them is Andrew, and the first thing he does is find his brother Simon: “We have found the Messiah.” He brings him to Jesus. Andrew is the patron of everyone who brings a brother or sister to Christ.

Paul writes to the Galatians with a mother's tenderness: “My little children, for whom I am again in the pain of childbirth until Christ is formed in you.” Evangelisation is not only information; it is labour and love until Christ takes shape in another person. On the eve of the Christmas fast, we prepare for Christ to be born, not only in Bethlehem but in us.

2026-11-30.question: Whom can I bring to Jesus?

homily: Dear friends, today is the feast of Mar Andrews Shleeha, St Andrew the Apostle. Two disciples of John the Baptist hear him say, look, here is the Lamb of God, and follow Jesus. He turns and asks: what are you looking for? Rabbi, where are you staying? Come and see, he says, and they remain with him that day. Andrew first finds his brother Simon and tells him: we have found the Messiah; and he brings him to Jesus (John 1:36–42).

Paul writes to the Galatians with a mother's heart: my little children, for whom I am again in the pain of childbirth until Christ is formed in you (Galatians 4:19). Bringing others to Christ carries the pain of love.

In this week after the Sunday of the Visitation, like Mary who went in haste to Elizabeth, like Andrew who ran to his brother, let us bring Christ to someone. Say to one person: come and see, to a prayer, to a Holy Qurbono. Amen.
